review_notes: I read the whole target file, which is one theorem. I also read the FiniteLaw expectation lemmas in KMedian/Probability/FiniteLaws.lean, SparseIntegerLaw.real_expect_all in SparseMixture.lean, step_expectation, and the sibling uses in RationalPhysicalSurvival.lean and RationalPhysicalCount.lean. I could not run Lean. I make no claim that simp loops or fails, and the suggested replacements are untested. The two findings are modest. They are about missing canonical simp lemmas and attributes, not defects in the mathematics. I did not recommend `@[simp]` on arbitrary identities. The `@[simp]` suggestion for the expectation linearity lemmas depends on whether adding it would disturb other files, which I did not check.

findings.excerpt:
rw [← SparseIntegerLaw.real_expect_all]
  have hpoint : ∀ G, (ν G).expectation (v G)=(ν G).real.expect (v G) :=
    fun G => (SparseIntegerLaw.real_expect_all (ν G) (v G)).symm
  simp_rw [hpoint]
findings.problem: `SparseIntegerLaw.real_expect_all` is stated as `μ.real.expect f = μ.expectation f`, which rewrites `real.expect` into `expectation`. This proof, and the same proofs in RationalPhysicalSurvival.lean and RationalPhysicalCount.lean, need the reverse, from `expectation` to `real.expect`. Each of the three therefore repeats the same steps. It uses `rw [← real_expect_all]` for the outer law. It then proves a local `hpoint` with `.symm` for the inner law under the binder. Then it runs `simp_rw [hpoint]`. SparseMixture.lean uses the lemma in its stated direction, as `simp only [FiniteLaw.prob, real_expect_all, ...]`. So the file base has no lemma whose orientation matches its main use, and no single normal form for expectations of sparse integer laws.
findings.proposed_change: Add a reverse lemma next to `real_expect_all`, for example `SparseIntegerLaw.expectation_eq_real_expect : μ.expectation f = μ.real.expect f`. The right-hand side contains no `expectation`, so the rewrite cannot loop. Then replace lines 92–96 with `simp only [SparseIntegerLaw.expectation_eq_real_expect]` followed by `exact hfinish`. This rewrites the outer and inner expectations in one pass. Alternatively, add a lemma specific to `step_expectation` that states the nested form directly in terms of `real.expect`. Use the new lemma in the two sibling files too.
findings.benefit: The per-use `hpoint` and `.symm` boilerplate goes away in three theorems. Each call site becomes one `simp only`. Readers get a documented orientation for turning sparse-law expectations into `FiniteLaw` expectations.

findings.excerpt:
simp_rw [FiniteLaw.expect_add,FiniteLaw.expect_const,FiniteLaw.expect_mul] at hav
  rw [FiniteLaw.expect_add,FiniteLaw.expect_const] at hav
findings.problem: `FiniteLaw.expect_add`, `expect_const`, `expect_mul`, `expect_sub` and `expect_mul_right` are the canonical linearity rules for expectations. None carries `@[simp]` or belongs to any simp set. Every caller, including this proof, lists them by hand. The call here needs `simp_rw` followed by a separate `rw` with a partly repeated list. `simp_rw` does not re-fire on the sum that the first pass produces, so a second pass is needed. In the sibling files, explicit `FiniteLaw.expect_*` rewrites appear in many other proofs.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the linearity lemmas `expect_add`, `expect_sub`, `expect_const`, `expect_mul` and `expect_mul_right` as `@[simp]` in FiniteLaws.lean. Alternatively, define a named simp set such as `finite_law_expect` containing them. Then lines 71–72 become one `simp only [FiniteLaw.expect_add, FiniteLaw.expect_const, FiniteLaw.expect_mul] at hav`. Every rule oriented this way rewrites `expect` of a compound function into a combination of simpler `expect`s, so the set terminates. `expect_mul` and `expect_mul_right` match different multiplication shapes, so they do not compete. Check the bulk of existing `simp` calls before adding the global attribute. The named set is the safer option.
findings.benefit: Callers get a single canonical normal form for expectations of linear combinations. The two-step rewrite and its hand-maintained rule lists in this proof and in the many files that use the same lemmas become one call.

evidence.excerpt: μ.expect (fun ω => f ω + h ω) = μ.expect f + μ.expect h
μ.expect (fun ω => c * f ω) = c * μ.expect f
μ.expect (fun ω => f ω * c) = μ.expect f * c
